title: Customer ops notice track and RCA milestone register
creator: Marissa Chen
description: Consolidate customer-facing communications and internal RCA milestone tracking for the 2026-03 capacity regression that caused cross-region throttling and degraded response rates. This ticket centralizes: (a) status update cadence for customers and internal stakeholders, (b) ownership and deadlines for RCA artifacts, and (c) action-item tracking until closure. The aim is to ensure consistent external messaging, reduce duplicated outreach, and capture technical remediation steps for future prevention.
incident_summary: On 2026-03-04 at ~03:10 UTC a change to the kernel memory layout in runtime-1.22 interacted with autoscaler thresholds causing unexpected pod evictions in eu-west-1 and us-central-1. Evictions reduced available capacity and triggered higher latency and rate-limited responses for hosted API customers for ~90 minutes. Root cause appears to be increased per-model KV cache memory footprint combined with conservative scale-up panics in the autoscaler. Impact: intermittent 5-20% error rate for affected requests and elevated token latency across multiple customer workloads.
timeline: 2026-03-04 03:08 UTC - Deploy of runtime-1.22 kernel optimization (PR #4827)
2026-03-04 03:12 UTC - Pager alert: region eu-west-1 node eviction storm
2026-03-04 03:15 UTC - On-call and infra team acknowledge; initial mitigation: increase pod restart backoff and disable aggressive preemption
2026-03-04 03:30 UTC - Temporary customer rate-limits applied to free/low tiers to preserve capacity for paid customers
2026-03-04 04:20 UTC - Rolling rollback of kernel optimization to 1.21 on affected pools completed
2026-03-04 04:40 UTC - Error rates returned to baseline; follow-up monitoring enabled
2026-03-05 10:00 UTC - Post-incident triage; preliminary RCA assigned to runtime & autoscaler teams
actions_taken: Rolled back kernel change on shared hosted pools (runtime-1.21) to restore stability
Applied interim rate limits for low-tier plans to protect committed capacity while capacity recovered
Increased autoscaler upper threshold and adjusted scale-up cooldown to avoid cascade during bursty evictions
Deployed additional KV cache instrumentation to measure per-model memory usage
Opened emergency PR to expose per-pool alloc metrics to SRE dashboards (PR #4856)

notes: Trade-off: rolling back kernel change resolved evictions quickly but postpones a planned optimization; engineering agreed to reintroduce after targeted staging tests and autoscaler changes

Learning: KV cache per-model variability was underestimated; require per-model memory profiling during model onboarding
